newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo, Gencor to access 230 Tonnes gold.
newsitem.headline: Anglo, Gencor to access 230 Tonnes gold.

text.p: A rationalisation of mineral rights between the gold operations of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and Gencor Ltd will make an additional 230 tonnes of gold accessible, the groups announced on Friday.
They said in a joint statement that existing operating gold mines, namely Beatrix, Oryx, Evander and Vaal Reefs, would be able to extend their operations by access to contiguous ground.

"Gencor and Anglo, as advisers to the parties, calculate that the recoverable gold in Weltevreden and 'Area One East' is in excess of 115 tonnes (3.7 million ounces) and this is matched in the southern Free State and Evander areas," the firms said.

Among the benefits for Gengold, Gencor's gold division, is the potential addition of about two million resource ounces to its Beatrix mine, which the parties said was the lowest cost producer in the industry.
Gengold would also receive the potential advantages of the contiguity of the area to Beatrix and Oryx mines, and potential additional reserves of about 1.7 million resource ounces to Evander.

Bobby Godsell, AngloGold's chief operating officer, said the bottom line for Vaal Reefs would be access to an additional 115 tonnes (3.7 million ounces of gold), which he said the mine should be able to exploit without significant additional infrastructure and within the immediate future.

In terms of the agreement Vaal Reefs has acquired from Anglo, Anglo American Gold Investment Co Ltd (Amgold) and associates, for a consideration of 416,400 Vaal Reefs shares, certain mineral rights contiguous to Beatrix and Oryx mines in the southern Free State.
It has also aquired certain mineral rights within or contiguous to the existing lease area of the Evander gold mines, the statement said.
Vaal Reefs has agreed to exchange these mineral rights for Gengold's 76.6 percent shareholding in Weltevreden Mines Ltd, which is contiguous to Vaal Reefs North Lease area.

At the same time Anglo, Amgold and associates have agreed to exchange certain mineral rights in the Evander area for Gengold's 66.2 percent stake in Gencor's 'Area One East' mineral rights holdings on the western boundary of the Vaal Reefs South Lease area.

Tom Dale, Gengold's managing director, was enthusiastic about the benefits of the deal for primary stakeholders in the gold mining industry. "I compliment industry leaders who are actively pursuing commercially logical mineral rights exchange," he said.

In a separate announcement, AngloGold said the tribute agreement with Weltevreden Mines which Vaal Reefs intends entering into would see it mining the area commencing in 1998 and turning to account at least an additional 68 tonnes (2.2 million ounces) of gold over 17 years.
In terms of this agreement Vaal Reefs will receive 55 percent of the revenue and pay 55 percent of the costs and capital expenditure, with the remaining 45 percent accruing to Weltevreden.

AngloGold said the area was expected to yield at least 10.6 million milled tonnes at an average recovered grade of 6.4 g/t. Working costs were estimated at 215 rand a tonne with capital expenditure required to bring the resource to account at 221 million rand in 1997 terms.

No agreement had been concluded with Anglo, Amgold and associates regarding 'Area One East' as further evaluations needed to be conducted to arrive at a mine plan and value for this area, the statement said.
AngloGold said Vaal Reefs had an eight percent stake in Weltevreden and an offer would be made to minority shareholders based on the value established for the swap with Gengold.
